environment.host: macOS local development environment without NVIDIA GPUs

evidence: The backend owns the immutable model ID, revision, public gdn-inside ID and runtime defaults.
Topology tests select non-adjacent PIX pairs when they are better than adjacent GPU numbers.
Plan tests produce four TP2 instances over all eight GPUs, disable the conflicting old deployment and remove the stale gdn-inside alias.
Unsafe host RAM and model-disk fixtures disable one-click deployment before any task starts.
Stale registry submissions fail closed and Qwen jobs persist before their background thread starts.
Qwen jobs start PLE workers sequentially, require per-instance real inference before publication and retain the pre-deployment backup for explicit rollback.
Admin-only HTTP routes map qwen38 plan and deploy requests to the model-control allowlist.
Six composable tests cover server-owned preset loading, one-click plan and submit, and the dedicated rollback action.
56 frontend tests passed across 9 files.
The Vite production build passed with 30 transformed modules.
280 Python tests passed in 55.660 seconds.
Shell syntax, Python compilation, strict JSON, git diff whitespace and source-size gates passed.
The online-upgrade ZIP initially failed because its test fixture omitted the two new runtime modules. The fixture was updated, and both original failed archive gates then passed.
model_deployment.py remains below the 3000-line limit; topology and resource logic is split into qwen38_deployment.py.

The default state showed Ornith 1.5 to Qwen3.8, gdn-inside retention, four TP2 groups, recommended parameter summaries and one enabled start button.
Advanced settings and all generic deployment tools were closed by default.
At a 390×844 viewport, innerWidth and document scrollWidth were both 390 with no horizontal overflow.
A successful deployment fixture hid the start button, displayed the Qwen online state and exposed the restore-to-pre-deployment button.
No browser console errors or warnings were reported.
